prompt.context: Our client, Clean Inc., is a manufacturer of heavy-duty soap with most of its £200m in revenues concentrated in Europe and the US. They sell soap to four client segments: healthcare, industry, commercial, and food. They have asked us to help them think about potential growth opportunities in both their existing markets and elsewhere.
prompt.question: The case has four parts: (1) Size the UK market for Clean's heavy-duty soap products using a bottom-up approach. (2) Identify potential growth opportunities for Clean. (3) Evaluate the strategic implications and expected profitability of a new electronic group monitoring system for soap usage. A data table (Exhibit 1) will be provided to support the market sizing.

clarifying_info.q: What is Clean's market share in the UK?
clarifying_info.a: Clean has a 40% market share in the UK.

clarifying_info.q: What is the penetration rate of heavy-duty soap in the UK by segment?
clarifying_info.a: In the UK, the penetration rate is 100% across all segments for this case.

clarifying_info.q: Are there specific segments or geographies to focus on?
clarifying_info.a: Start with the UK, which represents 20% of Clean's sales. The four segments are healthcare, industry, commercial, and food.

exhibits.title: UK Market Sizing Data Table
exhibits.shows: A table with columns for the four client segments (healthcare, industry, commercial, food) and rows for inputs needed to estimate market size. Some cells are pre-filled and others are left blank for the candidate to estimate.
exhibits.data: Four client segments: healthcare, industry, commercial, food. Rows include: number of employees (users of soap), usage per person per day, spend per usage, spend per employee per year, and total market size per segment.

exhibits.title: Information for Part 3 — Electronic Monitoring System
exhibits.shows: A data box with key assumptions about the new electronic group monitoring system product, covering global market size projections, market share of the group monitoring format versus individual tracking systems, investment requirements, product margins, and payback horizon.
exhibits.data: Global electronic monitoring market size: £10m (2014), £50m (2018), £250m (2025); Group monitoring share of market: 60% (remainder are individual tracking systems with badges); Investment required: £5m in 2014, £2m every year afterwards; Margins of product: 30%; Margins of Clean total: 25%; Payback time horizon: 5 years

framework: Approach the case in four parts: market sizing, growth opportunities, new product strategic assessment, and new product profitability
Market sizing: bottom-up — Market Size = Number of Employees (users) × Spend per Employee, broken out by segment
Growth opportunities: use a 2×2 of New vs Existing Products crossed with Existing vs New Customers (Ansoff), overlaid with Domestic vs International dimension
New product: assess market opportunity, competitive landscape, investment required, profitability (margin and NPV/IRR), and strategic fit before running the numbers

questions.prompt: Part 2: How would you size the UK market for Clean's heavy-duty soap products?
questions.guidance: Introduce both bottom-up and top-down approaches and discuss tradeoffs. Select bottom-up: Market Size = Number of Employees × Spend per Employee. Break each input down by segment (healthcare, industry, commercial, food). Spend per Employee = Usage per Person per Day × Spend per Occasion × ~250 working days. Candidate should proactively estimate blanks in Exhibit 1 using sensible assumptions. Bonus: distinguish MSP from RSP in value sizing; note penetration rate (100% in UK); sense-check result using Clean's 40% UK market share and personal experience on soap usage scaled for heavy-duty context; mention external factors such as regulation, health scares, and innovation.

math.setup: Market Size per segment = Employees in segment × Spend per employee per year. Spend per employee = Usage occasions per day × Spend per occasion × 250 working days. Sum across four segments for total UK market.
steps: Estimate employees in each segment in the UK (pre-filled or candidate-estimated from Exhibit 1)
Estimate soap usage per employee per day and cost per use per segment (heavier in healthcare and food than commercial/industry)
Spend per employee per year = usage per day × spend per occasion × 250 working days
Multiply employees × spend per employee per segment and sum totals
Sense-check: Clean's 40% UK share × total market should approximate £40m (20% of £200m revenues), implying total UK market ≈ £100m
math.answer: Total UK market approximately £100m, derived by summing segment estimates; validated by Clean's £40m UK revenues at 40% market share.

questions.prompt: Part 3A: How would you think about the ways that Clean could grow?
questions.guidance: Introduce a structured growth framework. A 2×2 of New vs Existing Products crossed with Existing vs New Customers (Ansoff matrix) works well. Layer in a Domestic vs International angle. Identify growth drivers as either Price (Spend per Employee) or Volume (Usage per Employee). Bonus: note that the number of employees in Industry is likely to decline due to automation, which reduces volume outlook for that segment.

questions.prompt: Part 3B: Can you identify specific growth opportunities within each area of your framework?
questions.guidance: Open-ended — no single correct answer. Strong answers generate concrete, distinct ideas per quadrant: e.g., (Existing product / New customers) enter new geographies or underserved segments; (New product / Existing customers) sell the electronic monitoring system or complementary hygiene products; (New product / New customers) develop consumer retail lines; (Existing product / Existing customers) drive volume through compliance programs or long-term contracts. Mention both organic and inorganic (M&A or licensing) options.

questions.prompt: Part 4A: What will be the impact of the new electronic group monitoring system for the company, the market, and Clean's strategy?
questions.guidance: Structure the answer to cover: size of opportunity (potential market); time horizon for payback; investment required; profitability of the product; IRR/NPV or internal go/no-go threshold; expected market share of Clean; other competitors; competing product types (e.g., individual badges on users); sectors to which this product would be attractive (especially healthcare given compliance costs); demand and expected take-up. Bonus: highlight external drivers such as the high regulatory cost of low hand-washing compliance in healthcare settings.

questions.prompt: Part 4B: Based on Exhibit 3, what are the expected profits by 2018 if Clean decides to go ahead with this product?
questions.guidance: Assume linear market growth from £10m (2014) to £50m (2018). Apply 60% group monitoring share, then 60% Clean market share, to get Clean revenues per year. Sum 2014–2018 revenues, apply 30% product margin for gross profit, subtract total investment (£5m + 4×£2m = £13m) to get net profit. Note 25% return as a positive signal.

math.setup: Annual Clean revenue = Total market size × 60% (group monitoring share) × 60% (Clean share). Gross profit = cumulative revenues × 30% margin. Net profit = gross profit − total investment.
math.answer: Net profit of £3.2m over 2014–2018, representing a 25% return on the £13m investment.

brainstorming.prompt: What are specific growth opportunities for Clean across each area of your growth framework (new vs existing products, new vs existing customers, domestic vs international)?

categories.name: Existing product / Existing customers
ideas: Increase usage frequency through hygiene compliance or training programs
Offer long-term bulk purchasing contracts with volume discounts
Upsell premium formulations or larger-capacity dispensers

categories.name: Existing product / New customers
ideas: Enter new geographies (e.g., emerging markets in Asia or Latin America)
Target underserved segments such as hospitality, education, or transportation
Supply white-label product to distributors or private-label retailers

categories.name: New product / Existing customers
ideas: Launch the electronic group monitoring system for compliance management
Develop complementary hygiene products such as hand sanitisers and disinfectants
Offer data analytics or reporting services built on usage monitoring data

categories.name: New product / New customers
ideas: Develop a consumer-grade soap line for retail channels
Sell IoT-enabled dispensers directly to facility managers
License the monitoring technology to other hygiene product companies

categories.name: International / Inorganic
ideas: Acquire regional soap manufacturers for scale and local distribution
Form joint ventures with local distributors in underpenetrated markets
License the Clean brand to local producers in markets where direct entry is costly

recommendation: Clean should pursue a dual-track growth strategy: expand geographically with its existing soap products in underpenetrated international markets, and invest in the electronic monitoring system given a positive expected return of £3.2m (25%) over five years
The monitoring system is especially compelling for healthcare, where regulatory pressure around hand-washing compliance creates strong pull demand
risks: The monitoring market is nascent and growth projections may be optimistic; competition from individual badge-based tracking could erode the assumed 60% group monitoring share
Geographic expansion requires local regulatory expertise, distribution partnerships, and potential product reformulation
Automation trends may shrink the industrial employee base over time, reducing soap volume in that segment
next_steps: Conduct a competitive analysis of the electronic monitoring market, focusing on badge-based alternatives and other entrants
Expand monitoring system pilots beyond the two initial hospitals before committing the full £13m investment
Prioritise geographic expansion markets using a market attractiveness screen (size, competitive intensity, regulatory environment)
